1.content: Create a native desktop app with TypeScript and open your first window.

2.content: macOS 14 or later Bun 1.4 or later TypeScript 7 Xcode Command Line Tools ( xcode-select --install ) macOS is the supported target today.

3.content: init writes the project and installs dependencies. Omit --language to choose Go, TypeScript, or Rust interactively.

4.content: reopen opens a window again when the user clicks the Dock icon and none are visible.

5.content: dev rebuilds as you edit. build writes a packaged app under dist/ .

6.content: Write components . Keep them in sync with signals . Add styles and layout .

7.content: The files in a QuickGUI TypeScript project and how to configure them. A TypeScript project keeps application code in app.tsx and development commands in package.json .

8.content: Keep reusable components in ordinary TypeScript modules. Build output lives in .quickgui ; packaged apps live in dist .

9.content: Import app and Window from @quickgui/native . Import components and createRenderer from @quickgui/solid . Await app.whenReady() before opening windows. Each window has its own renderer, disposed when the window closes.

10.content: The application icon comes from resources/icon.png . Extra files can be listed in resources . See App Icon and Bundled Resources . TOML supports the same keys. In tsconfig.json , set jsx to "preserve" and jsxImportSource to "@quickgui/solid" .

11.content: Applications depend on @quickgui/native , @quickgui/solid , and solid-js . @quickgui/cli is a development dependency. Terminal and updater are optional packages — see Auto Updater and Authoring Extensions .

12.content: check typechecks the project. test runs tests with the same compiler as builds.

13.content: Write components in JSX and use the built-in control set. Return JSX from ordinary functions. Put layout, typography, and color in style .

14.content: <View> accepts text directly. <div> and <span> are aliases for View and Text . There is no class or className ; everything visual goes in style .

15.content: View , Text , Button , Input , TextArea , Image , Svg , Shader , and VirtualList are the building blocks. TextInput is the same as Input . Terminal is available when you add the terminal package. bun add @quickgui/extension-editor adds Editor , CodeBlock , and DiffView . bun add @quickgui/extension-markdown adds Markdown .

16.content: Keep parts under the root they belong to so focus and values stay connected.

17.content: Pass the current value and a change callback, or use defaultValue , defaultChecked , and defaultOpen when the component can own its state.

18.content: The component reference covers forms, overlays, menus, tables, trees, and more. This repository includes examples/components-typescript as a gallery.

19.content: Apply style on each visible part. Parts ship unstyled so colors and layout belong to your app. Hooks such as useTabsState and useSelectState expose the current state for custom presentation.

20.content: Keep UI in sync with Solid signals, memos, and effects. Components run once when they mount. Read signals in JSX to update only the text or properties that depend on them.

21.content: A read during setup is a snapshot. Call the signal in JSX when the value should stay live.

22.content: Use createMemo for a value computed from other signals. Keep the function pure; write from events or effects.

23.content: Use createEffect for work outside the tree. Register onCleanup so subscriptions stop when the window closes or the branch is removed.

24.content: Solid batches ordinary signal writes. Use flush() in tests when you need queued updates to settle before an assertion.

25.content: Show and hide content, render lists, and work with the current window. JSX builds native UI, not HTML. Use Show and For when children should appear, disappear, or reorder as state changes.

26.content: A component function runs once. Solid updates the properties and child slots that read changing values. Each window has its own root, disposed when the window closes.

27.content: Removing a branch disposes its effects. Sibling content is left alone.

28.content: Give stateful rows a stable identity so reordering keeps their state. For long collections, use Table or Tree .

29.content: Each Window has an independent root. Closing one window does not close the others. Handle the Dock icon by opening a new window when hasVisibleWindows is false.

30.content: Capture the window during setup, or pass it into async work. Do not look it up from an unrelated callback later.

31.content: examples/components-typescript is the UI gallery. examples/quick-git-typescript is a larger app with menus, dialogs, and multiple windows.

32.content: Lay out and style views with Flexbox, Grid, and interaction states. Put every layout, typography, and color declaration in style , using camelCase keys. Lengths are logical pixels.

33.content: Boolean presets cover the same helpers as Go: roundedLg is an 8-pixel radius; p3 is 12 pixels. Custom values use borderRadius , padding , gridTemplateColumns , and width . A falsey preset ( false , null , or undefined ) turns that preset off.

34.content: Style arrays merge left to right. Later fields override earlier ones. Falsy entries are ignored. Removing a field from a reactive style object clears that property.

35.content: Keep getters in JSX when the value should update.

36.content: Use display , flexDirection , flexGrow , flexShrink , flexBasis , alignment, and gap. Set minWidth: 0 or minHeight: 0 on flexible scroll children so they can shrink.

37.content: Use display: "grid" with track, placement, and span fields.

38.content: Font family, weight, size, wrapping, and selection apply to text. Colors accept hex, CSS color strings, or packed RGBA values.

40.hierarchy: Styling & Layout › Groups and named group hover
40.content: Name a group on an ancestor and use groupHover or groupActive on descendants so they style together.

41.content: Build text fields, checkboxes, radios, and select controls. Keep field values in signals and write accepted changes back from event handlers.

42.content: onSubmit handles Return in a single-line input.

43.content: Field connects a label, control, description, and error.

44.content: Compose Checkbox , CheckboxGroup , RadioGroup , Radio , and Switch with their indicators and labels. Update state from each root’s change callback.

45.content: Select chooses from a list. Combobox mixes typing and selection. Autocomplete accepts free-form input.

46.content: Text events put the string in event.value . Buttons use onClick . Keep UI updates in those handlers; run slow work elsewhere and write signals when it finishes.

47.content: Show popovers, dialogs, and operating-system file pickers. Use a QuickGUI overlay for app-styled content, or a system dialog for file picking and alerts.

48.content: The side is a preference; placement flips if it would overflow.

50.content: SystemPopover opens a native child window, which can extend past the owner window’s edge. Give the content a width and height.

52.content: Declare routes, nested layouts, and in-app navigation. Declare routes, render the match in the current window, and navigate with links or useNavigate .

54.content: Nested routes are relative to their parent. Render <Outlet /> where the next matched route belongs. A pathless route can provide a shared layout without adding a URL segment.

55.content: The router supports push, replace, back, and forward. Navigation stays inside the app.

56.content: useLocation() and useSearchParams() also return reactive objects. Read location.pathname and searchParams.tab in JSX so the text stays current.

57.content: Animate hover, color, and opacity, and play GIF or WebP images. Animate style changes with transition on the base style. The component does not rerun for each frame.

59.content: Change a style from state and keep the node mounted. Do not rebuild the component on each frame.

60.hierarchy: Transitions & Animation › Timing and frame rate
60.content: Durations accept milliseconds or strings such as "180ms" . Set easing and maxFps when you want a cap. Omit maxFps to follow the display.

61.content: Color, border, radius, opacity, shadow, and transform interpolate. Width, height, and padding do not.

62.hierarchy: Transitions & Animation › Mounting and reduced motion
62.content: Keep an overlay mounted during its exit transition when the component supports that. Show removes children immediately. Transitions follow the system Reduce Motion setting. Set reduceMotion on the window to override it.

63.content: Image plays GIF and WebP files from the path you pass. You do not need a timer.

64.content: Open windows and use menus, clipboard, dialogs, and file watching. Create windows after app.whenReady() . Each window has its own UI root.

65.content: onClose and on("closed", ...) run after the window is gone. onCloseRequested can hold a close so you can ask the user to save. whenReady() resolves after the native window exists, including hidden windows. Handle the Dock icon with app.on("reopen", ...) and open a window when hasVisibleWindows is false.

66.hierarchy: Windows & Native Services › Commands and services
66.content: Calls that return a value are promises. Menus, file dialogs, clipboard, appearance, notifications, and tray icons are available from @quickgui/native . See Tray Icon .

67.hierarchy: Windows & Native Services › Events and file watching
67.content: Window events include focus, resize, appearance, minimize, fullscreen, and close. Application events include ready, reopen, activation, quit, and open URLs. Use Bun file watching for project files, and stop watchers in onCleanup when they belong to a window.

68.content: Embed real SwiftUI controls inside a TypeScript application. Import SwiftUI controls from @quickgui/solid/swift-ui and wrap them in Host . Ordinary QuickGUI components work without this.

69.content: The host is the native view boundary and can size itself from its content.

70.content: Buttons, labels, toggles, sliders, steppers, progress views, gauges, text and secure fields, pickers, segmented controls, date and color pickers, and popovers. They look and behave like the system controls.

72.content: matchContents sizes the host from the control. Per-axis options are available when you need a fixed width and an intrinsic height.

73.content: SwiftUI hosting requires macOS. Optional appearances such as Liquid Glass depend on the operating-system version.

74.content: Style SwiftUI controls and nest QuickGUI content inside them. Modifiers style native SwiftUI controls. Reverse hosting puts QuickGUI content inside SwiftUI.

75.content: Import factories from @quickgui/solid/swift-ui/modifiers and pass them in order. They include control size, tint, disabled state, label style, button border shape, and button style.

76.content: macOS draws glass where it is available.

78.content: Use Popover.Trigger with a SwiftUI control and Popover.Content for the presented UI. A QuickGUIHostView inside that content hosts ordinary QuickGUI children.

79.content: An embedded host closes with its owner. Unmounting removes the native view; do not keep a detached host through a global subscription.

80.content: Use resources/icon.png as the packaged application icon, or change the window or Dock icon at runtime. The packaged application icon is the image Finder, the Dock, the Windows taskbar, Start Menu, and Linux desktop launchers show for your app. Put a PNG at resources/icon.png . You can also change a window icon or the macOS Dock icon while the app is running.

81.content: Add a square PNG that is at least 256×256 pixels at resources/icon.png . 1024×1024 is a good source. quickgui build resizes it to every size macOS, Windows, and Linux need. The CLI writes .icns for macOS, .ico for the Windows installer, and the Freedesktop hicolor sizes for Linux. Development reloads skip generated containers; production builds and a configured macos.icon still install an icon. Optional resources/icon.iconset/icon_<n>x<n>.png files replace a generated size with a hand-drawn one. That folder is a build input and is not copied into the packaged app. Set icon in the CLI config only when the source PNG lives somewhere other than resources/icon.png .

82.content: Use these when you already have a platform container: resources/icon.icns is used on macOS when macos.icon is omitted. resources/icon.ico is used by the NSIS installer when windows.icon is omitted. linux.icon is a square PNG used when both resources/icon.png and icon are omitted. macos.icon must be an .icns . windows.icon is an .ico . These config paths override the files in resources/ . Document-type icons are a basename inside the packaged resources. See Bundled Resources .

83.hierarchy: App Icon › Window and Dock icons
83.content: The packaged icon is the application identity. A window can show a different image on Windows and X11: iconPath is an absolute filesystem path. Join it from app.getPaths() as shown in Bundled Resources . After the window exists, call window.setIcon(iconPath) or window.clearIcon() . On macOS, windows do not have their own icon. Use app.dock.setIcon(iconPath) to replace the Dock image for this process. Menu-bar and notification-area icons are a different image. See Tray Icon .

84.content: Target Sizes macOS .icns 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 Windows .ico 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256 Linux hicolor 16, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256, 512 Every listed size is generated from the source PNG. The source must be square, at least 256×256, and at most 16 MiB.

85.content: Add a menu-bar or notification-area icon, and mark macOS template images by filename or flag. A tray icon lives in the macOS menu bar, the Windows notification area, or a Linux StatusNotifierItem host. Put the artwork in resources/ and create the icon after app.whenReady() . This is separate from the packaged App Icon .

86.hierarchy: Tray Icon › Create a tray icon
86.content: Ship a small PNG with the app, then create the icon from its packaged path: Tray.create assigns an id. Call tray.update , tray.showMenu , or tray.destroy on that handle. Tray is supported on macOS, Windows, and Linux. A 22×22 PNG is a good 1× source. Draw a 44×44 companion as trayTemplate@2x.png when you want a retina menu-bar image.

87.content: On macOS, a template image is a monochrome mask. AppKit recolors it for the menu bar's light, dark, and highlighted appearances using only the alpha channel. A filename whose stem ends in Template , optionally followed by @2x or @3x , is treated as a template: trayTemplate.png and statusTemplate@2x.png match. emailTemplateIcon.png does not. Pass { path, template: true } or iconIsTemplate: true when the name does not follow that convention, or { path, template: false } to force the flag off. The same template field applies to window icons, Dock icons, about-panel icons, and menu item icons. Other platforms keep the flag and ignore it.

88.content: The tray menu is a native context menu. Action items call click . Listen for click , double-click , enter , move , leave , menu-item , and scroll on tray.on . showMenu opens the menu at the cursor on macOS and Windows. Linux hosts own menu presentation and reject that call.

89.content: Platform Host Template images showMenu macOS Menu bar extra Recolored by AppKit Supported Windows Notification area Ignored Supported Linux StatusNotifierItem Ignored Unsupported Tray.isSupported() is true on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Keep at most 32 tray icons.

90.content: Ship files in resources/ and load them from the packaged resource directory. Put application files that are not compiled into the executable in a resources/ directory: images, templates, JSON, and other data. The CLI copies that directory’s contents into the packaged app. The running app reads them from the resource directory, which does not depend on the launch working directory. Custom fonts are a separate option. See Fonts .

91.content: Each file keeps its path relative to resources/ . resources/hero.png is installed as hero.png . resources/copy/template.txt is installed as copy/template.txt . Destination names must not replace reserved names such as fonts , AppIcon.icns , quickgui.json , or the host shared library. quickgui dev and quickgui build both stage these files. A missing extra path listed in config fails the build. The resources/ directory itself is optional.

92.content: Use the resources config option to merge extra files or folders into the same packaged directory. Each extra path is copied under its basename. Do not list the project resources/ folder here; it is included automatically. legal/NOTICE.txt is installed as NOTICE.txt . vendor/data is installed as data/ .

93.content: Platform Resource directory macOS .app Contents/Resources Linux AppDir, AppImage, and .deb Next to the executable ( usr/bin ) Windows installer Next to the executable in $INSTDIR Join packaged names onto resourceDir at runtime; do not read from the project tree or the current working directory.

94.content: Await app.whenReady() , then join the packaged name onto resourceDir : Image accepts that filesystem path. Other files use the same join: read them with Bun.file or readFileSync . Relative image paths are not resolved against the resource directory.

95.content: fonts lists OpenType files. The CLI copies them into fonts/ inside the resource directory and registers them before the first window opens. Use the font family name in style . Fonts are not a replacement for resources/ : an image or JSON file still belongs in that directory or in the extra resources list.

96.content: Ship signed automatic updates for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Install @quickgui/extension-updater to include automatic updates. Apps that omit it do not ship the updater.

97.content: Generate a signing key pair and copy the public key into the project: Keep the private quickgui-update.key out of version control. A darwin-arm64 build checks https://downloads.example.com/my-app/appcast-darwin-arm64.xml unless you set updates.feedUrl . {target} in that URL is replaced with the current target.

98.content: Start after app.whenReady() , outside components, so every window shares one session:

99.content: API Use updater.check() Manually check for an update. updater.install() Install an available update. updater.setAutomaticChecks(enabled) Change the automatic-check preference. updater.state Read the last event. updater.close() Stop a session the app no longer needs. Status is idle , checking , available , downloading , installing , or disabled . Closing a window must not close the shared updater. Development builds report disabled by default. Use { allowDevelopment: true } only with a test feed and a disposable app bundle.

100.content: macOS uses Sparkle. Windows uses a signed NSIS installer. Linux uses an AppImage. Linux package-manager installs report disabled . Current prebuilt packages cover macOS; other targets need a native build on that host.

101.content: Increase version in quickgui.config.ts . Load the private key into the environment: Upload the versioned archive first, then the appcast. Each architecture has its own feed. updates.manifest: true generates a feed on every production build.

102.content: From this repository, build the updater once with bun packages/native/build.ts --extension updater . Packaged apps include it when the extension is listed in config.

103.content: Share Solid components or add a native service your app can call. Extensions can provide ordinary Solid components, retained native components, or asynchronous native services. Editor, Markdown, and Terminal are optional component packages; Updater is an optional service. Third-party packages use the same SDK without changing quickgui-host .

104.hierarchy: Authoring Extensions › Choose an extension type
104.content: Use an ordinary TypeScript package for reusable Solid UI. Use a native component when its state or rendering logic belongs in Rust, or a native service for asynchronous operations. Native libraries run in the application's existing process and use its renderer; they do not bundle another host.

105.hierarchy: Authoring Extensions › Create an extension project
105.content: TypeScript apps consume the same native packages as Go. --npm-package sets the artifact package name.

106.content: Publish the package and add it as an application dependency.

107.hierarchy: Authoring Extensions › Lay out a native extension
107.content: A combined extension can be both a Go module and an npm package. Put Rust in src/ , TypeScript in js/ , and built libraries in lib/<platform>-<arch>/ . The root manifest names your package, independent version, ABI, and library. See the Go authoring guide and the first-party extensions/ packages.

108.content: Custom extensions may use a scoped name such as @acme/extension-echo .

109.hierarchy: Authoring Extensions › Implement the native contract
109.content: Native components implement create , update , render , event , and destroy . Rust authors use Component , ComponentFactory , and ComponentRuntime from quickgui-extension-sdk , which has no renderer dependency. Render stable keyed primitives, request only visible virtual rows, and wake only the owning instance when background work completes. Release state and wake handles when it is destroyed. A TypeScript binding mounts the registered component and supplies reactive properties: onEvent(kind, value, event) receives the component's output; the binding owns its typed public API. The host never interprets package-specific properties. Native services instead implement invoke and shutdown . Copy borrowed input before returning, keep events scoped to their sessions, and release workers when a session stops.

110.content: The CLI bundles declared extensions. The app loads them at startup, so components can call them after app.whenReady() .

111.hierarchy: Authoring Extensions › Build and package artifacts
111.content: Rebuild the native library when its implementation changes, then rebuild the app. Resources listed in the manifest are copied next to the library. Export js/index.ts from the npm package. Keep @quickgui/* and Solid in peerDependencies , with development copies in devDependencies ; do not bundle another QuickGUI runtime. Extension READMEs contain build instructions only; the user guide belongs on the website.

112.content: Test against a packed extension in a fresh project. Confirm that an app without the package does not bundle the library.

134.content: A retained native code editor with syntax coloring, line numbers, indentation, and both-axis scrolling. No language grammars are included by default. Register a linked grammar in Rust, or load one portable pack of selected Tree-sitter Wasm grammars and queries using loadLanguagePack (TypeScript) / LoadLanguagePack (Go). Unstyled by default: text and line-number colors inherit, and the component adds no background, border, rounding, padding, or syntax/diff palette. Supply application styles and explicit colors to opt into an appearance.
134.keywords: Primitives Value Language LineNumbers TabSize ReadOnly OnChange

137.content: language selects a registered Tree-sitter grammar and highlight query. Query captures map through syntaxTheme to eight foreground-only paint classes, so color never changes text metrics. Source or language changes reparse the bounded document; palette changes only remap retained captures, and scrolling does no syntax work. Parsing is limited to 2 MiB, individual lines over 32 KiB stay plain, and the capture count is capped. This does not require a language server.

139.content: Selectable, caret-free source code with Tree-sitter coloring and virtualized logical rows. No language grammars are included by default. Register a linked grammar in Rust, or load one portable pack of selected Tree-sitter Wasm grammars and queries using loadLanguagePack (TypeScript) / LoadLanguagePack (Go). Unstyled by default: text and line-number colors inherit, and the component adds no background, border, rounding, padding, or syntax/diff palette. Supply application styles and explicit colors to opt into an appearance.
139.keywords: Primitives Value Language LineNumbers Wrap SyntaxTheme

142.content: language selects a registered Tree-sitter grammar and highlight query. Captures map through syntaxTheme to foreground-only spans, so highlighting does not change layout. The Rust core parses when source or language changes; scrolling only mounts logical rows and materializes their precomputed spans. Parsing is limited to 2 MiB, individual lines over 32 KiB stay plain, and the capture count is capped.

144.content: A virtualized split or unified file diff with synchronized rows and independent pane scrolling. No language grammars are included by default. Register a linked grammar in Rust, or load one portable pack of selected Tree-sitter Wasm grammars and queries using loadLanguagePack (TypeScript) / LoadLanguagePack (Go). Unstyled by default: text and line-number colors inherit, and the component adds no background, border, rounding, padding, or syntax/diff palette. Supply application styles and explicit colors to opt into an appearance.
144.keywords: Layout & Data Patch OldText NewText OldPath NewPath Options Theme

147.content: DiffView uses the same registered Tree-sitter grammars as Editor. When its document, language, or syntax palette changes, the Rust core parses each visible old/new file lane once and assigns capture fragments to logical rows. Styled text is materialized and cached only when a row is mounted, with inline addition/deletion emphasis merged at non-overlapping byte boundaries. Scrolling never invokes the parser.

A single- or multiple-choice picker whose option surface is rendered in a native popover window.
A virtualized hierarchical collection with expansion, selection, and keyboard navigation.

A virtualized split or unified file diff with synchronized rows and independent pane scrolling. No language grammars are included by default. Register a linked grammar in Rust, or load one portable pack of selected Tree-sitter Wasm grammars and queries using loadLanguagePack (TypeScript) / LoadLanguagePack (Go). Unstyled by default: text and line-number colors inherit, and the component adds no background, border, rounding, padding, or syntax/diff palette. Supply application styles and explicit colors to opt into an appearance.
A virtualized tabular collection with header, row, and cell parts.

Add a menu-bar or notification-area icon, and mark macOS template images by filename or flag. A tray icon lives in the macOS menu bar, the Windows notification area, or a Linux StatusNotifierItem host. Put the artwork in resources/ and create the icon after app.whenReady() . This is separate from the packaged App Icon .

Add a square PNG that is at least 256×256 pixels at resources/icon.png . 1024×1024 is a good source. quickgui build resizes it to every size macOS, Windows, and Linux need. The CLI writes .icns for macOS, .ico for the Windows installer, and the Freedesktop hicolor sizes for Linux. Development reloads skip generated containers; production builds and a configured macos.icon still install an icon. Optional resources/icon.iconset/icon_<n>x<n>.png files replace a generated size with a hand-drawn one. That folder is a build input and is not copied into the packaged app. Set icon in the CLI config only when the source PNG lives somewhere other than resources/icon.png .

An accessible press target that you style and compose with text or other content.
An embedded host closes with its owner. Unmounting removes the native view; do not keep a detached host through a global subscription.
An in-window modal with focus containment, dismissal, and exact transition completion.
An on/off control with a root track and independently styled thumb.
Animate hover, color, and opacity, and play GIF or WebP images. Animate style changes with transition on the base style. The component does not rerun for each frame.

API Use updater.check() Manually check for an update. updater.install() Install an available update. updater.setAutomaticChecks(enabled) Change the automatic-check preference. updater.state Read the last event. updater.close() Stop a session the app no longer needs. Status is idle , checking , available , downloading , installing , or disabled . Closing a window must not close the shared updater. Development builds report disabled by default. Use { allowDevelopment: true } only with a test feed and a disposable app bundle.

Applications depend on @quickgui/native , @quickgui/solid , and solid-js . @quickgui/cli is a development dependency. Terminal and updater are optional packages — see Auto Updater and Authoring Extensions .
Apply style on each visible part. Parts ship unstyled so colors and layout belong to your app. Hooks such as useTabsState and useSelectState expose the current state for custom presentation.

DiffView uses the same registered Tree-sitter grammars as Editor. When its document, language, or syntax palette changes, the Rust core parses each visible old/new file lane once and assigns capture fragments to logical rows. Styled text is materialized and cached only when a row is mounted, with inline addition/deletion emphasis merged at non-overlapping byte boundaries. Scrolling never invokes the parser.
Displays a filesystem path, file URL, or base64 data URL with retained image resources.
Displays a scalar measurement within a known range and semantic low, high, and optimum bands.
Durations accept milliseconds or strings such as "180ms" . Set easing and maxFps when you want a cap. Omit maxFps to follow the display.

Each file keeps its path relative to resources/ . resources/hero.png is installed as hero.png . resources/copy/template.txt is installed as copy/template.txt . Destination names must not replace reserved names such as fonts , AppIcon.icns , quickgui.json , or the host shared library. quickgui dev and quickgui build both stage these files. A missing extra path listed in config fails the build. The resources/ directory itself is optional.
Each Window has an independent root. Closing one window does not close the others. Handle the Dock icon by opening a new window when hasVisibleWindows is false.

Font family, weight, size, wrapping, and selection apply to text. Colors accept hex, CSS color strings, or packed RGBA values.

fonts lists OpenType files. The CLI copies them into fonts/ inside the resource directory and registers them before the first window opens. Use the font family name in style . language selects a registered Tree-sitter grammar and highlight query. Captures map through syntaxTheme to foreground-only spans, so highlighting does not change layout. The Rust core parses when source or language changes; scrolling only mounts logical rows and materializes their precomputed spans. Parsing is limited to 2 MiB, individual lines over 32 KiB stay plain, and the capture count is capped.

language selects a registered Tree-sitter grammar and highlight query. Query captures map through syntaxTheme to eight foreground-only paint classes, so color never changes text metrics. Source or language changes reparse the bounded document; palette changes only remap retained captures, and scrolling does no syntax work. Parsing is limited to 2 MiB, individual lines over 32 KiB stay plain, and the capture count is capped. This does not require a language server.
Lay out and style views with Flexbox, Grid, and interaction states. Put every layout, typography, and color declaration in style , using camelCase keys. Lengths are logical pixels.
Lays out and paints the visible part of a long or variable-height collection. Mounts only the visible slice of a long or variable-height collection.

Name a group on an ancestor and use groupHover or groupActive on descendants so they style together.

Native components implement create , update , render , event , and destroy . Rust authors use Component , ComponentFactory , and ComponentRuntime from quickgui-extension-sdk , which has no renderer dependency. Render stable keyed primitives, request only visible virtual rows, and wake only the owning instance when background work completes. Release state and wake handles when it is destroyed. A TypeScript binding mounts the registered component and supplies reactive properties: onEvent(kind, value, event) receives the component's output; the binding owns its typed public API. The host never interprets package-specific properties. Native services instead implement invoke and shutdown . Copy borrowed input before returning, keep events scoped to their sessions, and release workers when a session stops.

On macOS, a template image is a monochrome mask. AppKit recolors it for the menu bar's light, dark, and highlighted appearances using only the alpha channel. A filename whose stem ends in Template , optionally followed by @2x or @3x , is treated as a template: trayTemplate.png and statusTemplate@2x.png match. emailTemplateIcon.png does not. Pass { path, template: true } or iconIsTemplate: true when the name does not follow that convention, or { path, template: false } to force the flag off. The same template field applies to window icons, Dock icons, about-panel icons, and menu item icons. Other platforms keep the flag and ignore it.

onClose and on("closed", ...) run after the window is gone. onCloseRequested can hold a close so you can ask the user to save. whenReady() resolves after the native window exists, including hidden windows. Handle the Dock icon with app.on("reopen", ...) and open a window when hasVisibleWindows is false.

Rebuild the native library when its implementation changes, then rebuild the app. Resources listed in the manifest are copied next to the library. Export js/index.ts from the npm package. Keep @quickgui/* and Solid in peerDependencies , with development copies in devDependencies ; do not bundle another QuickGUI runtime. Extension READMEs contain build instructions only; the user guide belongs on the website.
Removing a branch disposes its effects. Sibling content is left alone.

reopen opens a window again when the user clicks the Dock icon and none are visible.

Shapes and paints Unicode text with inherited typography, selection, and accessibility.

Share Solid components or add a native service your app can call. Extensions can provide ordinary Solid components, retained native components, or asynchronous native services. Editor, Markdown, and Terminal are optional component packages; Updater is an optional service. Third-party packages use the same SDK without changing quickgui-host .

Ship a small PNG with the app, then create the icon from its packaged path: Tray.create assigns an id. Call tray.update , tray.showMenu , or tray.destroy on that handle. Tray is supported on macOS, Windows, and Linux. A 22×22 PNG is a good 1× source. Draw a 44×44 companion as trayTemplate@2x.png when you want a retina menu-bar image.

Ship files in resources/ and load them from the packaged resource directory. Put application files that are not compiled into the executable in a resources/ directory: images, templates, JSON, and other data. The CLI copies that directory’s contents into the packaged app. The running app reads them from the resource directory, which does not depend on the launch working directory. Custom fonts are a separate option. See Fonts .
Ship signed automatic updates for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Install @quickgui/extension-updater to include automatic updates. Apps that omit it do not ship the updater.
Show and hide content, render lists, and work with the current window. JSX builds native UI, not HTML. Use Show and For when children should appear, disappear, or reorder as state changes.
Show popovers, dialogs, and operating-system file pickers. Use a QuickGUI overlay for app-styled content, or a system dialog for file picking and alerts.
Shows a richer hover or focus preview beside a trigger without changing the current screen.
Shows an image with a fallback that appears when the image is unavailable.
Shows and hides one panel from a trigger while preserving accessible state.
Shows passive help after an exact core-owned delay and supports provider-level warm-up behavior.

The application icon comes from resources/icon.png . Extra files can be listed in resources . See App Icon and Bundled Resources . TOML supports the same keys. In tsconfig.json , set jsx to "preserve" and jsxImportSource to "@quickgui/solid" .
The CLI bundles declared extensions. The app loads them at startup, so components can call them after app.whenReady() .
The component reference covers forms, overlays, menus, tables, trees, and more. This repository includes examples/components-typescript as a gallery.
The concealed native editor with the same controlled contract as TextField.
The confirmation-focused dialog variant with stricter backdrop-dismissal defaults.
The files in a QuickGUI TypeScript project and how to configure them. A TypeScript project keeps application code in app.tsx and development commands in package.json .
The host is the native view boundary and can size itself from its content.
The multiline text-editing primitive, with the same controlled value contract as Input.
The NSHostingView-backed leaf that mounts one SwiftUI component tree inside QuickGUI.

The packaged icon is the application identity. A window can show a different image on Windows and X11: iconPath is an absolute filesystem path. Join it from app.getPaths() as shown in Bundled Resources . After the window exists, call window.setIcon(iconPath) or window.clearIcon() . On macOS, windows do not have their own icon. Use app.dock.setIcon(iconPath) to replace the Dock image for this process. Menu-bar and notification-area icons are a different image. See Tray Icon .
The router supports push, replace, back, and forward. Navigation stays inside the app.
The side is a preference; placement flips if it would overflow.

The tray menu is a native context menu. Action items call click . Listen for click , double-click , enter , move , leave , menu-item , and scroll on tray.on . showMenu opens the menu at the cursor on macOS and Windows. Linux hosts own menu presentation and reject that call.

TypeScript apps consume the same native packages as Go. --npm-package sets the artifact package name.

Use an ordinary TypeScript package for reusable Solid UI. Use a native component when its state or rendering logic belongs in Rust, or a native service for asynchronous operations. Native libraries run in the application's existing process and use its renderer; they do not bundle another host.
Use createEffect for work outside the tree. Register onCleanup so subscriptions stop when the window closes or the branch is removed.
Use createMemo for a value computed from other signals. Keep the function pure; write from events or effects.
Use display , flexDirection , flexGrow , flexShrink , flexBasis , alignment, and gap. Set minWidth: 0 or minHeight: 0 on flexible scroll children so they can shrink.
Use display: "grid" with track, placement, and span fields.
Use Popover.Trigger with a SwiftUI control and Popover.Content for the presented UI. A QuickGUIHostView inside that content hosts ordinary QuickGUI children.

Use resources/icon.png as the packaged application icon, or change the window or Dock icon at runtime. The packaged application icon is the image Finder, the Dock, the Windows taskbar, Start Menu, and Linux desktop launchers show for your app. Put a PNG at resources/icon.png . You can also change a window icon or the macOS Dock icon while the app is running.

Use the resources config option to merge extra files or folders into the same packaged directory. Each extra path is copied under its basename. Do not list the project resources/ folder here; it is included automatically. legal/NOTICE.txt is installed as NOTICE.txt . vendor/data is installed as data/ .

Use these when you already have a platform container: resources/icon.icns is used on macOS when macos.icon is omitted. resources/icon.ico is used by the NSIS installer when windows.icon is omitted. linux.icon is a square PNG used when both resources/icon.png and icon are omitted. macos.icon must be an .icns . windows.icon is an .ico . These config paths override the files in resources/ . Document-type icons are a basename inside the packaged resources. See Bundled Resources .
useLocation() and useSearchParams() also return reactive objects. Read location.pathname and searchParams.tab in JSX so the text stays current.

View , Text , Button , Input , TextArea , Image , Svg , Shader , and VirtualList are the building blocks. TextInput is the same as Input . Terminal is available when you add the terminal package. bun add @quickgui/extension-editor adds Editor , CodeBlock , and DiffView . bun add @quickgui/extension-markdown adds Markdown .
